I am playing Monopoly.

I am p2 with $61 cash. I own three hotels on ST_CHARLES_PLACE, STATES_AVENUE, and VIRGINIA_AVENUE.

I also own two get-out-of-jail cards and two mortgaged railroads. The opponent has massive holdings across multiple monopolies and $1090 cash. Two other players are bankrupt. This is a one-on-one endgame with very little money.

I am on Baltic Avenue. I just paid rent there. I will roll from this position next turn.

Rolling a 2 lands on Income Tax. I cannot pay the $200 tax with only $61. Other rolls hit my own hotels or mortgaged properties.

Rolling a 4, 6, or 7 would cost $550 to $600 in rent. Selling a hotel returns only half its purchase price. That is too little cash to survive these rolls.

Selling all three hotels would raise $750. I cannot mortgage or unmortgage anything right now because both the mortgageable and unmortgageable lists are empty.

I am deciding whether to sell my hotels preemptively. My previous strategy avoided pre-selling because the pink monopolies are the only weapon to force the opponent off dark blue properties. I now have only $61 cash, and rolling a 2 on my next turn would hit Income Tax for $200.

I can likely survive these rolls by selling buildings only when the debt actually arrives, rather than pre-selling. Selling one hotel returns $50, which still leaves a gap against the $200 Income Tax.

The opponent is on Atlantic Avenue. Their next roll cannot land on my pink hotels, since those spaces are St Charles, States, and Virginia. I will not be forced off my dark blue properties this turn.

The opponent is 25 spaces away from St Charles, so they cannot land on my pink hotels this turn. They still have $1090 and four houses on the red properties, leaving two hotels to build. Only two hotels remain in the bank.

Hoteling two red properties would cost $150 each, and the opponent has enough cash to do it. That would raise rent on Kentucky, Indiana, and Illinois to over $1000, which would be devastating. I cannot stop them from building hotels on their own turn. The only remaining option is to end the turn and keep my current holdings.

I am now considering a trade with p1. I could offer my pink hotels, but the opponent might not want them if they are about to bankrupt me. I also have Tennessee mortgaged, which would complete their orange set and give them a monopoly. I still hold two get-out-of-jail cards and two mortgaged railroads.

A trade with p1 is unlikely to help. They have $1090 and multiple monopolies, so they do not need my pink hotels or get-out-of-jail cards. They would not break their own dark blue, red, or light blue monopolies for cash. Selling the pink monopoly would eliminate my only weapon against them, and the cash I might receive would not be enough to survive their board.

I am now calculating exact rent amounts to determine how much cash I need to survive. Brown hotels cost $250 and $450. Light blue hotels cost $550, $550, and $600. My pink hotels are actually worth $750 each, not $600. The opponent's red properties at four houses cost $625 each. I need to know these precise figures before deciding whether to sell buildings.

Virginia hotel rent is $900. Kentucky and Indiana hotels are $1050 each. Illinois hotel is $1100. Park Place hotel is $1500 and Boardwalk hotel is $2000. Almost every unmortgaged property on the board is a hotel that can bankrupt me with only $61 cash.

The only viable strategy is to keep the pink hotels and hope the opponent lands on them before I land on their dark blues. The opponent is still far from my pink properties.

From Baltic, rolling a 2 hits Income Tax for $200. That might be manageable if I liquidate buildings first. Rolling a 4, 6, or 7 would hit Oriental, Vermont, or Connecticut hotels for $550 to $600. Those rolls would force immediate liquidation.

Rolling a 4, 6, or 7 next turn carries a 14 in 36 chance of hitting light blue hotels for $550 to $600. Liquidating all three pink hotels would raise $750, plus the $61 cash, giving $811 total. That covers the rent but leaves me with no hotels and mortgaged Tennessee and PRR.

Selling two full hotels for $500 and one downgrade for $50 would raise $550. That leaves me with $11 and one hotel, which is enough to survive the light blue rent but still leaves me defenseless against Park Place, Boardwalk, or other high-rent properties. I am checking whether this engine allows selling buildings during a debt resolution phase.

I am now calculating the exact cost to unmortgage the opponent's orange properties. St James, New York, and Tennessee each mortgage for $90, but unmortgaging them costs $99, $110, and $99 respectively. Building houses on those spaces would cost $100 each.

Unmortgaging the opponent's orange properties would require too much cash to be worthwhile. They have no incentive to trade because they already hold enough money and are not in jail. I am now considering whether proposing a bad trade would waste my turn or if it would still allow me to take another action.

I am now weighing whether to propose a trade at all. The engine would apply the result and ask again if more actions remain legal, but I can only make one tool call per turn. I considered offering my pink hotels in exchange for cash or immunity, yet the opponent has $1090 and would not give up their dark blue monopolies.

The opponent might actually want to buy my pink hotels to eliminate the threat, since they have $1090 and could afford it. But mortgaged properties do not charge rent, so they would not help me avoid rent. Cash is the only way to survive their hotels. I need roughly $1700 just to cover the light blue hotels on one circuit.

The total rent for one full circuit exceeds $8000. Cash from a trade cannot cover that. The only viable path is to keep the pink hotels and force the opponent to downgrade their dark blue and red properties before I die.
